rendering_opacity_slider.note: opacity 0.3 from the slider; as layer_rendering_tab

rendering_cdf_click.note: the range's nearer end to 195, the lower bound focused (the row is a <label>); as layer_rendering_tab

rendering_type_bound.note: range [100, 195] typed; the caret's blink phase; as layer_rendering_tab

seg_render_tab.note: radios, sliders, the render scale histogram, light checkboxes

seg_segments_tab.note: starred list: star/eye states, the hidden segment's icons off the pointer

seg_segment_query.note: an ID query: its list and the starred list sharing the height; the caret's blink phase

seg_annotations_tab.note: the data bounds in global coordinates

image_annotations_tab.note: as seg_annotations_tab, for the image layer

rendering_range_finder.note: 5-95% gives [10, 244] as in neuroglancer (the CPU-sampled histogram's iteration); the CDF line's sampling noise

json_state_editor.note: the overlay at half pixels (transform), CodeMirror with folds; the fold markers' glow is approximated

screenshot_dialog.note: the framed dialog (settings, preview tables, progress); the long description's antialiasing

statistics_panel.note: docked at the bottom by `\\`, captured once neuroglancer has re-ranked its chunks for the smaller panels (500 ms after the key it still counts the 14 the full-height panels wanted; settled, both count 12). Counts and memory match (raw uint32 segmentation at neuroglancer's compressed-segmentation size, 2636 bytes): 503 px when the latencies print alike. Not pixel-perfect by nature: the download latencies are wall-clock times (masked), and a latency string longer or shorter than neuroglancer's moves the table's columns (~5200 px)

add_layer.note: a new layer, its Source tab with the URL focused and the stores' completions; the caret's blink phase

add_layer_typed.note: named from the URL, the URL made canonical, its subsources unused (struck), Create as … bars

command_palette.note: the catalog (layer groups, commands with their bindings, tools); the shortcut symbols' fallback font (the focused panel's white border goes with the keyboard to the palette's input: `:focus-within`)

command_palette_search.note: prefix matches first, the second active (the focused panel's white border goes with the keyboard to the palette's input: `:focus-within`)

segment_dblclick_show.note: a double-click on segment 71 shows (and stars) it; the list's icons differ as in seg_segments_tab

segment_dblclick_hide.note: a second double-click hides it, still starred (`!71`); icons as in seg_segments_tab

segment_dblclick_unstar.note: Shift+double-click unstars it; icons as in seg_segments_tab

segment_entry_hover.note: the entry under the pointer is the hovered segment: highlighted in the panels, its entry #222; icons as in seg_segments_tab

mesh_4panel.note: the same in the 4-panel layout's 3D panel, behind the slices; line antialiasing, checkbox corners, 2 glyph pixels

mesh_3d.note: legacy precomputed meshes of seg_mesh (8 segments, one hidden) in 3D, exact; the data-bounds lines' antialiasing where they cross a mesh and 2 glyph pixels differ

mesh_move_to_segment.note: right-click on segment 106's entry: to its loaded mesh's vertex nearest the position (40, 13.8, 12); neuroglancer then prefetches (the layer items' bottom strips), which this viewer does not; list icons as in seg_segments_tab

mesh_move_no_mesh.note: right-click on hidden segment 82's entry: no mesh loaded: the temporary message, identical; list icons as in seg_segments_tab

boundary_position.note: the position exactly on the image's upper x bound: the last voxel shows (neuroglancer's closed chunk box and clamp), and the data-bounds face as one rectangle; line antialiasing differs

multires_3d.note: multi-resolution (Draco) meshes of seg_multires (two levels of detail); data-bounds line antialiasing and 2 glyph pixels differ

multires_far.note: the same zoomed out (meshRenderScale 1); line antialiasing and 2 glyph pixels

annotations_4panel.note: a local annotation layer (points, one off the plane and faded; a line on the plane and one crossing it; a box; an ellipsoid, filled at half alpha in cross-sections; a polyline with its vertex markers) in each panel, and its layer bar colour; line antialiasing, the box's edges where they overlap in 3D

annotations_3d.note: the same in 3D: points and line endpoints as circles, the box's edges and corners, the ellipsoid a lit 10×10 sphere; line antialiasing and overlapping edges at equal depth

annotation_layer_panel.note: an annotation layer's Source tab: local://annotations, the identity onto the global dimensions (unbounded), +S (a mutable source rank) and +V; text antialiasing

annotation_layer_rendering.note: its Rendering tab: the annotation shader (CodeMirror's 300 px, valid: green), Hide inactive shader controls, Annotation color; panel annotations' antialiasing

annotation_layer_list.note: the annotation layer's Annotations tab: the related-segment filters, the tools, help, Prev/Next, the header and each annotation's rows (floored coordinates, the type symbol); the toolbox glyphs sit half a pixel apart

annotation_layer_schema.note: the Schema tab without properties: the explanation (wrapped), download/upload/copy/paste, the header (Default value wrapping in its cell), add; panel annotations' antialiasing

annotate_point.note: Ctrl+click with the point tool: the point placed at the pointer, selected (the list's entry, the Selection panel's details), the tool in the top bar; the ID is random (masked); the toolbox's half-pixel offsets as in annotation_layer_list

annotate_box.note: the box tool: the first corner, the pointer moving, the second (z one more); selected again at each change (history: back), the list scrolled to it; the ID masked; toolbox offsets as in annotation_layer_list

skeleton_4panel.note: precomputed skeletons of seg_skeleton (8 segments, one hidden): lines and points in the cross-sections, lines in 3D; the data-bounds lines' antialiasing and 2 glyph pixels as in mesh_4panel

skeleton_3d.note: the same skeletons in the 3D layout; the data-bounds lines' antialiasing and 2 glyph pixels as in mesh_3d

skeleton_options.note: skeletonRendering: 2D lines 4 px without points, 3D lines and points 3 px, objectAlpha 0.7 (transparent: order-independent blending); differences as in skeleton_4panel

mesh_transparent.note: mesh_3d at objectAlpha 0.5: the meshes in the transparent pass, blended order-independently over the slices and lines

skeleton_render_tab.note: a segmentation layer with skeletons: Resolution (mesh) (none drawn), Opacity and Silhouette (3d), the skeleton modes and widths, the vertex attribute, the skeleton shader; radios, slider antialiasing and glyph offsets as in seg_render_tab

mesh_render_tab.note: a segmentation layer with meshes: Resolution (mesh) (manifests and fragments at an infinite scale), Opacity (3d), Silhouette (3d); differences as in seg_render_tab

skeleton_line_width.note: the 2D line width set to 21 by clicking its slider: thicker lines and points in the cross-sections, each segment's edges then its nodes (neuroglancer's segment order follows its randomly seeded hash set, so overlaps of different segments may differ between runs); the tab as in skeleton_render_tab

skeleton_mode_wheel.note: the 2D mode by wheel over its select (EnumSelectWidget's own listener): lines only; the tab as in skeleton_render_tab

skeleton_standalone.note: a skeleton directory as a source of its own (neuroglancer_skeletons info): a segmentation layer without a volume, in the default nanometre space

skeleton_standalone_source.note: its Source tab: the default subsource as skeletons, the identity onto x, y, z in nanometres (unbounded). multires_sharded.note: multires_3d with the manifests and fragments in shards (identity hash, 2 shards of 2 minishards): manifests by key, fragments by byte range before them

mesh_3d_hover.note: the pointer over a mesh in 3D: picked (the Z and pick buffers read around the pointer): its segment in the layer bar and highlighted, the position on its surface in the top bar

mesh_3d_dblclick.note: double-click on a mesh in 3D: its segment hidden

annotation_hover_line.note: the pointer over a line in the xy panel: picked within the pick radius, drawn three quarters of the way to white (the marker borders black); differences as in annotations_4panel

annotation_hover_box.note: the pointer over a box's cross-section edge in the xy panel: picked within the pick radius, drawn three quarters of the way to white (the marker borders black); differences as in annotations_4panel

annotation_select_position.note: Ctrl+right-click over a point (select-position): the selection pinned with the picked annotation (annotationId, annotationPart) and the position snapped onto it, the Selection panel showing its details; half-pixel glyph and icon offsets as in the other selection scenarios

annotation_move.note: Alt+drag over a point (move-annotation): it follows the pointer by its representative point (translateDataPointByViewportPixels), in every panel

channels_rgb.note: the channels as red, green and blue (getDataValue(0..2), channels stacked in the chunk texture)

channels_invlerp.note: an invlerp over channel 1 (#uicontrol invlerp normalized(channel=1))

channels_render_tab.note: a multi-channel image's Rendering tab: the channel dimensions (c^ [0, 3)), the invlerp's channel as a position under its label (c^ 1) and no legend; 1-2 px glyph offsets in the bounds and CDF sampling as in layer_rendering_tab

channels_hover.note: the pointer over a multi-channel image: every channel's value in the layer bar (96,40,120)

channels_type_channel.note: the invlerp's channel typed (2, Enter): the shader reads channel 2 (z), the field keeps the focus with its dropdown (the channel plot); otherwise as channels_render_tab

volume_rendering.note: an image volume-rendered (volumeRendering on, the default shader, 64 depth samples) in the 3D layout

volume_rendering_max.note: maximum intensity projection (volumeRendering max): per ray the sample of the greatest invlerp value

volume_rendering_4panel.note: volume rendering in the 4-panel layout: the rays stop at the slice planes (the Z buffer)

volume_rendering_gain.note: volumeRenderingGain 1.5 (alpha times e^1.5) and 128 depth samples (a finer scale's brightness factor)

volume_rendering_tab.note: the Rendering tab with volume rendering on: Gain (3D), Resolution (3D) (depth samples, the chosen scale's bar and the others' indicators)

precomputed_points_sparse.note: the same with 60 px cross-section and 90 px projection spacing: the coarse level's cell and part of the fine level's (drawFraction) per view

precomputed_points_tab.note: its Source tab: the default subsource as annotations, the identity onto the collection's x, y, z and bounds (text antialiasing differs by a few pixels)

precomputed_points_annotations_tab.note: its Annotations tab: the cross-section and projection spacing widgets (prompt, histogram, legend) above an empty, read-only list without the toolbox or a segments relationship. Known: the histogram canvases (66 px bitmaps over 65.7 and 85.69 px boxes at x 1040.55, 1020.56) are resampled by Chrome with a filter this viewer's fractional boxes only approximate (~350 px)

precomputed_points_hover.note: the pointer over a precomputed point in the yz panel: picked, drawn three quarters of the way to white

precomputed_points_select.note: Ctrl+right-click over a precomputed point: the selection pinned with the annotation (its decimal id), the position snapped onto it, the Selection panel showing its details and properties

precomputed_points_by_id.note: a selection in the state of a precomputed point in a cell not drawn at 60/90 px spacing: fetched from the by_id index for the Selection panel (geometry and properties)

n5_4panel.note: an N5 multiscale group (s0 gzip, s1 blosc, s2 zstd; per-scale downsamplingFactors) as an image layer, the finest scale in view

n5_coarse.note: the same zoomed out: coarser scales (blosc, zstd blocks) chosen

n5_source_tab.note: its Source tab: the canonical URL (|n5:), the default and bounds subsources, x y z in nanometres with the base scale's bounds (text antialiasing differs by a few pixels, as in the other Source tabs)

deepzoom_png.note: a Deep Zoom image (300 × 200, 64 px PNG tiles, 1 px overlap) as an RGB image over its c^ channels: neuroglancer's PNG tiles transposed twice (decompressPng makes them planar, the tile source again), reproduced

deepzoom_coarse.note: the PNG pyramid zoomed out: coarser levels

precomputed_points_shader.note: an annotation shader over precomputed properties (setColor(prop_color()), setPointMarkerSize(prop_size()), white borders), evaluated per annotation in a compute pass

annotations_shader_controls.note: the annotation layer's Rendering tab with the shader's colour and slider controls (width at 2.5)

precomputed_points_rendering_tab.note: its Rendering tab: the property list (rgb prop_color(), float32 prop_size()) above the shader

precomputed_points_sharded.note: the same collection with its spatial levels in shards (cells by compressed Morton code)
